outcome: Experiment Authoring now has a real syntax-highlighted code editor foundation
owner_impact: Configuration, Initialization, Controller and Metrics are edited through a CodeMirror surface with line numbers, Python-like syntax highlighting, normal selection/undo/redo/clipboard behavior and preserved responsive styling. The existing artifact textareas remain the authoritative source buffers underneath, so dirty-state, autosave, Apply & restart, revision history and read-only Experiment behavior keep their established semantics.

next.text: #204 is the next code-authoring ergonomics ticket. It adds parser-derived outline/symbol navigation, folding and reliable in-artifact search on top of this editor foundation. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: CodeMirror is loaded through pinned browser modules and falls back to the existing textarea if editor initialization fails.
Only the deployed Python-like artifact formats receive Python syntax parsing/highlighting; no Virtual Lab scientific names are hardcoded as fake semantic tokens.
CodeMirror edits mirror into the authoritative textareas through the existing input contract, while authoritative Experiment/revision loads reset editor state without manufacturing dirty edits.
Read-only state is mirrored from the existing artifact textareas into CodeMirror.
The existing interaction-boundary autosave logic treats the CodeMirror surface as inside the artifact editor.
Production browser smoke requires four ready CodeMirror surfaces, hidden authoritative fallback textareas, line numbers and rendered highlighted tokens.
CodeMirror CDN imports disable esm.sh submodule bundling so shared CodeMirror state/view dependencies resolve as one module graph instead of duplicated extension identities.
Production smoke reports per-artifact CodeMirror initialization errors if the editor CDN graph fails again.
